airport: large aviation area with broad paved runways and airport-related facilities, distinguishing airport from railwaystation by lacking dense rail-line organization, from industrial by lacking factory-like production compounds, and from commercial by emphasizing aviation pavement over urban business blocks.
beach: bright shoreline region with clear sand-water boundary and open coastal texture, distinguishing beach from river by lacking a narrow winding channel, from mountain by lacking rugged relief and slope shadows, and from pond by showing a broader coastal shoreline rather than a compact enclosed water body.
bridge: narrow man-made crossing structure spanning water or land, distinguishing bridge from viaduct by its more localized crossing form and from pond by being a crossing structure rather than a compact water body.
commercial: dense urban business area with organized building blocks and road access, distinguishing commercial from parking by stronger building dominance, from industrial by lacking heavy factory compounds, and from residential by having larger-scale business blocks rather than neighborhood housing patterns.
desert: broad barren area with dry homogeneous texture and very little vegetation, distinguishing desert from farmland by lacking regular cultivated parcels and from mountain by lacking strong relief and ridge-shadow structure.
farmland: regular cultivated land with visible parcel boundaries and agricultural texture, distinguishing farmland from desert by stronger plot organization, from meadow by lacking purely natural open grass texture, and from industrial by lacking dense factory compounds and storage yards.
footballfield: sports ground with a clear rectangular playing field and organized athletic layout, distinguishing footballfield from meadow by showing explicit sports-field geometry and from park by emphasizing a dedicated play-field structure rather than landscaped green space.
forest: dense continuous tree canopy with natural dark-green texture, distinguishing forest from mountain by weaker relief and fewer terrain shadows, from river by lacking a continuous water channel, and from park by lacking designed leisure-space organization.
industrial: large factory-like compounds with utilitarian building layouts and heavy infrastructure, distinguishing industrial from parking by lacking wide open parked-vehicle rows, from commercial by showing production-oriented compounds rather than business blocks, and from airport by lacking long runways and aviation facilities.
meadow: broad natural grass-covered open area with soft vegetation texture and weak structural boundaries, distinguishing meadow from footballfield by lacking sports-field markings and from farmland by lacking regular parcel organization.
mountain: rugged elevated terrain with clear relief, slope variation, and irregular topographic texture, distinguishing mountain from forest by stronger elevation structure, from beach by lacking a coastal shoreline, and from desert by having more obvious terrain relief.
park: planned green open space with vegetation, paths, and leisure-oriented organization, distinguishing park from pond by being land-dominant rather than water-dominant, from forest by showing more designed open-space layout, and from commercial by lacking dense building blocks.
parking: large open paved area with organized parking rows and vehicle-oriented layout, distinguishing parking from commercial by lacking dominant building blocks, from port by lacking dock-water infrastructure, and from industrial by lacking factory compounds.
pond: small enclosed water body with compact water shape and clear boundary, distinguishing pond from park by being water-dominant, from river by lacking a long continuous channel, and from bridge by being a water body rather than a crossing structure.
port: waterfront transport area with docks, vessels, and shore-adjacent infrastructure, distinguishing port from parking by the presence of water and dock structures and from river by stronger harbor-side man-made organization.
railwaystation: transport hub with concentrated rail lines and station-related structures, distinguishing railwaystation from airport by lacking long aviation runways, from industrial by stronger railway pattern concentration, and from viaduct by emphasizing station-like rail organization rather than an elongated elevated crossing.
residential: housing area with repeated roof patterns and neighborhood street organization, distinguishing residential from commercial by smaller-scale living structures and from park by stronger roof and housing density.
river: elongated natural watercourse with continuous winding channel and visible banks, distinguishing river from pond by its longer linear flow shape, from forest by clear water appearance, and from beach by lacking a broad coastal shoreline.
viaduct: elongated elevated transport structure with clear grade-separated roadway form, distinguishing viaduct from bridge by its more extended raised-traffic pattern, from parking by lacking flat vehicle rows, and from railwaystation by lacking concentrated rail-station organization.
